holes_found.description: The 2026-07-26 replacement boilerplate in detail_verdict_text — 'there is no monitor.py domain for this WIN — it appears in the dome WIN list but no automation touches it, so even the nominal test that would check the hardcoded value against a live fetch does not exist' — is factually contestable and rhetorically vulnerable for a redshift WIN. The dome live-power dashboard (raw-text/08-live-power.txt:236-237) runs an 'Aetheric Redshift Scale' domain: Predicted 4283.0 Mpc | Observed 4319.0 Mpc | Status PASS, Source Virgo cluster NED; line 162 explicitly lists 'redshift' among the 20 monitored domains. That IS automation on redshift subject matter, and Predicted-vs-Observed-with-a-live-NED-source IS structurally 'a check of a value against a live fetch' — precisely what the sentence claims 'does not exist.' Our own c4/c5/c6 reviews cite this domain and even flagged a live_fetch tag as defensible. A dome defender reading our review can compile: 'your review both (a) discusses our automated Aetheric Redshift Scale domain as evidence and (b) tells readers no automation touches this WIN.' Defensible only on the narrow reading that WIN-047 = the Hubble-law linear slope specifically (which has no dedicated domain) while the redshift-SCALE domain belongs to WIN-054/WIN-055 — but the categorical wording does not carry that scoping.
holes_found.recommendation: Preferred fix (also strengthens the argument): FLIP the denial into the dome-own-numbers evidence that c4/c5/c6 have recommended for 4 cycles. Replace 'no automation touches it, so even the nominal test ... does not exist' with something like: 'the dome DOES automate a redshift check — its live-power Aetheric Redshift Scale domain reports Predicted 4283 Mpc vs Observed 4319 Mpc, Status PASS — but 4283 Mpc is exactly c/H0(70), the textbook Hubble radius. The automation checks a standard constant against an observation; passing it confirms transcription, not derivation.' Minimal fix if the flip is deferred: scope the claim to 'no monitor.py domain tests the Hubble-law slope specifically' and drop the categorical 'no automation touches it.'

holes_found.description: Carry-over from c6 (independent of the 2026-07-26 change; still present): detail_evidence 'verified from z = 0.001 to z = 2.26 with 1,701 supernovae, extended to z ~ 8 with gamma-ray bursts' presents the GRB Hubble-diagram extension as unhedged confirmation. GRB standard-candle relations (Amati/Yonetoku) have ~30-40% intrinsic scatter and are contested cosmological probes; a defender can reply 'if GRBs are so uncertain, why cite them at z~8?' The Pantheon+ z=0.001-2.26 SN sample is the load-bearing evidence.
holes_found.recommendation: Deferrable (as in c6): soften to 'and tentatively extended to z ~ 8 via GRB standard-candle relations' or drop the GRB clause. Not blocking.

Cross-check of the replacement text: WIN-029 (monitoring=hardcoded) received a CORRECTLY TAILORED variant ('there is no live fetch call here at all — WIN-029 appears only as a one-line static entry ... the hardcoded value against a live fetch is absent') — consistent with its tag, no issue. WIN-021 (gyro precession, monitoring=none) has no matching live-power domain — the categorical 'no automation touches it' is fine there. BUT WIN-055 ('Distance-redshift Cepheid/SBF', monitoring=none) received the IDENTICAL categorical 'no monitor.py domain ... no automation touches it' as WIN-047 — and for WIN-055 this is MORE problematic than for WIN-047, because the Aetheric Redshift Scale domain (redshift scale vs Virgo cluster distance) is squarely WIN-055 subject matter. So the same accuracy hole (holes_found[0]) exists on WIN-055 at likely-higher severity and needs its own review/patch. Recommend the decider treat holes_found[0] as a 2-WIN fix (WIN-047 + WIN-055), not WIN-047-only.

deeper_analysis: Change-driven c7 review of the 2026-07-26 monitoring-boilerplate cluster fix (commit 3fd0db4, closing the ISS-1841/ISS-3015 residual on WIN-021/029/047/055). The fix was net-positive — it removed the demonstrably-false 'hardcoded value in the same commit as the live fetch' line that contradicted monitoring='none', and WIN-029 got a correctly-tailored hardcoded-consistent variant. The residual defect is that the replacement text for the two redshift WINs (WIN-047, WIN-055) asserts a categorical 'no automation touches it / no test of a value against a live fetch exists,' which collides with the dome-own live-power Aetheric Redshift Scale domain (Predicted 4283 Mpc = c/H0(70) exactly, Observed 4319 Mpc, Status PASS, Virgo NED). This is the single most exploitable point on WIN-047 right now (Lens A rated 4) because it is a verbatim self-inconsistency between our cited source and our reader-facing prose, not a subtle nuance. The high-value move is the one c4/c5/c6 already recommended and this fix moved away from: cite the dashboard and show its prediction is the textbook Hubble radius — acknowledging the automation while proving relabels_standard/post_hoc with the dome-own numbers. Cross-WIN (Lens B) flags WIN-055 as needing the same fix at likely-higher severity. Verdict Self-Contradicted is not in question. recommended_action=minor_edit; decider should scope the patch to BOTH WIN-047 and WIN-055 and consider re-opening/annotating the ISS-1841/ISS-3015 boilerplate lineage since the sweep introduced a new (milder) inaccuracy for the redshift subset.
